newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe wins confidence vote for austerity.
newsitem.headline: Juppe wins confidence vote for austerity.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe won a parliamentary vote of confidence on Wednesday for his austerity policies despite grumbling in his centre-right coalition.

Deputies in the National Assembly voted by 464 to 100 to endorse the embattled premier, officials said. The victory had been a foregone conclusion since Juppe's coalition controls four-fifths of the 577 seats.

There were four abstentions out of 568 votes cast. Juppe earlier rejected charges that he called the vote to silence dissent in his coalition in the run-up to 1998 elections. "This vote of confidence will not be a blank cheque," he said.
Almost all members of the ruling coalition voted for the government while the Socialists and Communists voted against. It was the third confidence vote Juppe has won since taking office in May 1995.
In policy statement earlier, Juppe promised a "new democracy" for the year 2000 and a drive for jobs amid record unemployment of 12.6 percent of the workforce.

"I believe perseverance will pay off and that 1997 will be a year of improvement," he said. He urged his allies to combat widespread gloom and convince voters that the government was on the right track.
